faq.question: What is Thymosin Alpha-1?
faq.answer: It is a synthetic 28-amino-acid peptide corresponding to residues 2–29 of human prothymosin α (CAS 62304-98-7), used as a research reagent in immunology.

faq.question: Is the sequence documented?
faq.answer: Yes — the product page states the sequence and precursor reference (UniProt P06454), and each batch is identity-confirmed by mass spectrometry.

faq.question: What is the difference between Thymosin Alpha-1 and TB-500?
faq.answer: They are unrelated peptides that both derive from larger precursor proteins: thymosin α1 comes from prothymosin α and is studied in immune signalling, whereas TB-500 (thymosin β4 fragment) is studied in actin-sequestration and cell-migration models.

faq.question: How is it stored and shipped?
faq.answer: Shipped as lyophilized powder in 10-vial kits; store desiccated at 2–8°C protected from light, and aliquot after reconstitution to avoid freeze–thaw cycles.
